Estimate suppressed death counts

Source: R/data-suppressed.R
mt_fill_suppressed.Rd

Official statistics often suppress small cells for confidentiality (for example "." in tables of the German Federal Statistical Office, "<3" or "<5" elsewhere) while publishing totals: deaths of a region over all causes, deaths of the whole country by cause. mt_fill_suppressed() estimates the missing death counts of the bottom strata from two sources of information:

Usage

mt_fill_suppressed(
  data,
  hierarchy = NULL,
  lower = 0,
  upper = Inf,
  maxit = 10000,
  tol = 1e-06
)

Arguments

data

An mt_data object in which some death cells are missing (cells that other strata have and that no observed cell of the stratum overlaps, so a stratum reported in other age groups is not filled; suppressed values are left out when the data are read).

hierarchy

An mt_hierarchy() that describes the published totals in the data, or NULL when there are none.

lower, upper

Bounds of the suppressed counts.

maxit, tol

Iterations and tolerance (in deaths) of the raking; cells are raked until no estimate changes by more than tol.

Value

The mt_data object with filled deaths; a summary in attribute "fill" (cells filled, cells left missing, inconsistent cells, iterations, largest relative gap to a published total).

Details

  • published totals (hierarchy): the missing cells of every aggregate with a known total must add up to that total minus its known cells. They are estimated by iterative proportional fitting (raking; Deming and Stephan 1940; Bishop, Fienberg and Holland 1975): starting values, the expected deaths at the pooled death rate of the same age and period, are scaled constraint by constraint until every total is matched. With two crossed variables (regions and causes) and no binding bounds, the limit is the fit of the log-linear model of independence (with the starting values as offset) to the missing cells given both margins (Bishop, Fienberg and Holland 1975). Missing aggregates are then filled as sums of their parts.

  • bounds of the suppressed counts (lower, upper): the range that the suppression rule implies, for example lower = 1, upper = 2 when counts of 1 and 2 are suppressed, or upper = 4 for "<5". During raking, the estimates are clipped to the bounds within each proportional-fitting step. This clipping is a heuristic of this package: once a bound binds, the result is no longer the log-linear fit above, and the iterations have no convergence guarantee (they stop after maxit, and a remaining gap to a published total is reported). Cells that no published total covers get the mean of a Poisson distribution with the expected deaths at the pooled rate as its mean, truncated to the bounds: E[Y | lower <= Y <= upper] over the integers in the range. This needs a finite upper.

Without bounds, cells that no published total covers stay missing (with a warning). The estimates are plausible values that agree with the published information; they carry no information beyond it, so forecasts of strata with many estimated cells are less certain than their intervals suggest. Filled cells are marked with provenance "estimated". When the known cells of an aggregate already exceed its total (inconsistent data), the missing cells of that aggregate are set to the lower bound and the case is reported.

References

Bishop YMM, Fienberg SE, Holland PW (1975). Discrete Multivariate Analysis: Theory and Practice. MIT Press.

Deming WE, Stephan FF (1940). On a least squares adjustment of a sampled frequency table when the expected marginal totals are known. Annals of Mathematical Statistics 11(4): 427-444.

Examples

d <- data.frame(region = c("A", "B", "C", "all"), year = 2020, age = "90+",
                deaths = c(10, NA, NA, 40), exposure = c(100, 200, 200, 500))
x <- mt_data(deaths = d, exposure = d, by = "region")
#> Warning: 2 missing deaths value(s) left out; suppressed counts can be estimated with mt_fill_suppressed().
y <- mt_fill_suppressed(x, mt_hierarchy(region = "all"))
mt_obs(y)
#>    stratum region  label age_lo age_hi period_lo period_hi value provenance
#>      <int> <char> <char>  <num>  <num>     <num>     <num> <num>     <char>
#> 1:       1      A      A     90    Inf      2020      2021    10   observed
#> 2:       2      B      B     90    Inf      2020      2021    15  estimated
#> 3:       3      C      C     90    Inf      2020      2021    15  estimated
#> 4:       4    all    all     90    Inf      2020      2021    40   observed
attr(y, "fill")
#>    filled missing inconsistent iterations max_gap
#>     <int>   <int>        <int>      <int>   <num>
#> 1:      2       0            0          2       0
# counts below 3 suppressed, no totals: Poisson mean truncated to 1-2
d2 <- data.frame(region = c("A", "B"), year = 2020, age = "90+", deaths = c(30, NA),
                 exposure = c(1000, 50))
z <- mt_fill_suppressed(mt_data(deaths = d2, exposure = d2, by = "region"), lower = 1, upper = 2)
#> Warning: 1 missing deaths value(s) left out; suppressed counts can be estimated with mt_fill_suppressed().
mt_obs(z)
#>    stratum region  label age_lo age_hi period_lo period_hi     value provenance
#>      <int> <char> <char>  <num>  <num>     <num>     <num>     <num>     <char>
#> 1:       1      A      A     90    Inf      2020      2021 30.000000   observed
#> 2:       2      B      B     90    Inf      2020      2021  1.428571  estimated
